summary: This paper presents a bang-bang protocol for nondispersive qubit readout using sudden quenches of the qubit-resonator coupling instead of adiabatic parameter sweeps. The protocol achieves fast, high-fidelity quantum-non-demolition readout with errors scaling as $1/N_\mathrm{eff}$ by exploiting dynamics in the Jaynes-Cummings model with a large photon number $N_\mathrm{eff}$.
motivation: Conventional dispersive readout limits the readout rate to $\sim g^2\sqrt{N}/\Delta \ll g$, while adiabatic approaches in the nondispersive regime ($g^2 N/\Delta^2 \gg 1$) encounter measurement-induced state transitions from multiphoton resonances. Eliminating parameter sweeps via sudden coupling quenches offers a route to fast, QND readout without these resonance crossings.
method: The authors develop an analytical theory for the Jaynes-Cummings model combining saddle-point approximation with systematic perturbation theory in $1/N_\mathrm{eff}$. A preloaded resonator couples suddenly to the qubit at strength $g$, pointer states separate at rate $g$ over readout time $t_r \approx 4g^{-1}$, then the coupling switches off for projective resonator measurement. The qubit post-measurement occupies time-dependent sweet-spot states $|\pm(t)\rangle$ with high purity.
result: At typical parameters ($g/2\pi \approx 100$ MHz, $\Delta/2\pi \approx 23$ MHz), readout times drop below 10 ns with QNDness and fidelity exceeding 99% at effective photon number $N_\mathrm{eff} \geq 11$, representing $>10\times$ speedup over dispersive readout while maintaining high-fidelity state preservation for mid-circuit measurements and reset.
